# Research questions and definitions

## Genuine Erdős number

An Erdős path is accepted only when every edge represents research
co-authorship and can be tied to a bibliographic source. Name similarity alone
is not evidence. Ambiguous identities and disputed edges are recorded rather
than silently resolved.

The initial outcome is the minimum verified path length for each researcher in
the study population, together with the full path and supporting publications.

## The “Erdős of Icelandic engineering”

This phrase is treated as a structural comparison, not a nickname assigned by
intuition. Candidate measures include:

- degree and weighted degree;
- betweenness and brokerage between institutions or fields;
- closeness or harmonic centrality in disconnected networks;
- eigenvector-like measures, where their assumptions fit the graph;
- robustness across time windows and reasonable population definitions.

Co-authorship and MSc co-supervision are first analysed as separate layers.
Any combined network must state how edge types and repeated collaborations are
weighted.

## Population still to define

The population definition is a research decision. It must specify the relevant
institutions, departments and disciplines; whether affiliation is current or
historical; the observation period; and how visiting or cross-appointed
researchers are handled.
